newsitem.title: ITALY: Italians acquitted of murder of American boy.
newsitem.headline: Italians acquitted of murder of American boy.

text.p: Two Italians were cleared on Thursday of murdering a seven-year-old American boy who became a hero in Italy after his death when his parents donated his organs to save the lives of six Italians.

A court in Catanzaro, southern Italy, acquitted Francesco Mesiano, 23 and Michele Iannello, 28, of murder for the shooting death of Nicholas Green during an attempted motorway robbery more than two years ago.
Both defendants denied any involvement in the shooting. The prosecution earlier this week had asked the court to impose prison terms of 23 years.

Nicholas was on holiday in Italy with his family, from Bodega Bay, California, when their hired car was chased and shot at on an isolated stretch of motorway in the southern Calabria region in an attempted hold-up. He was hit in the head as he slept on the back seat next to his sister.

The boy's father, Reginald, had returned to Italy to witness the verdict, which ended a nearly year-long trial. He and his wife Margaret, who recently had twin girls, earned deep respect in Italy with their decision to donate Nicholas's organs.

They were praised as humanitarian heroes by the media and left the country after the shooting with an award from President Oscar Luigi Scalfaro and pledges that hospitals, streets and schools would be named after their son.
